description.narrative: Moldavien står inför flera naturliga faror inklusive översvämningar, torka, jordbävningar, hagelstormar och extrem värme. Dessa faror utgör utmaningar för landets jordbrukssektor, infrastruktur och befolkningens allmänna välbefinnande.Även om klimatförändringarna förväntas öka Moldaviens sårbarhet, märks dess effekter redan i jordbrukssektorn och landets övergripande försörjning. Detta femåriga projekt med en total budget som täcks helt av Sida på 29 990 800 SEK syftar till att öka kapaciteten för hydrologiska, meteorologiska och klimatologiska informationstjänster vid Serviciul Hidrometeorologic de Stat (SHS) som nationell leverantör av meteorologiska, hydrologiska och klimatdata som samt varningar för katastrofrisk. Projektet Strengthening Hydrometeorological Capacity in Moldova (SHC Moldova) syftar till att stödja SHS i att stärka deras datahantering, prognoser och katastrofriskkommunikation med ett starkt fokus på digitalisering och automatiseringsprocesser.

Moldova faces several natural hazards including flooding, drought, earthquakes, hailstorms, and extreme heat. These hazards pose challenges to the country’s agricultural sector, infrastructure, and overall well­being of the population. While climate change is expected to increase the vulnerability of Moldova, its effects are already being felt in the agricultural sector and the country’s overall livelihood. This 5 years project with a total budget covered fully by Sida of 29 990 800 SEK aims to enhance the capacity for hydrological, meteorological and climatological information services at Serviciul Hidrometeorologic de Stat (SHS) as the national provider of meteorological, hydrological and climate data as well as disaster risk warnings. The Strengthening Hydrometeorological Capacity in Moldova (SHC­Moldova) project aims to support SHS in strengthening their data management, forecasting and disaster risk communication skills with a strong focus on digitalization and automatization processes.

The SHC-Moldova project aims to support SHS in strengthening their data management, forecasting and disaster risk communication skills with a strong focus on digitalization and automatization processes. The project will develop human technical capacity and improve weather and water information services, including forecast and early warning systems, as well as improve disaster risk communication and action. Good governance procedures form an integral part of the capacity development effort.
Project Outcome: - Enhanced capacity for hydrological, meteorological and climatological information services at SHS in its role as national provider of meteorological, hydrological and climate data as well as disaster risk warnings.
• Output 1 Strengthened capacity for information technology (IT). • Output 2 Strengthened capacity for management of historical data . • Output 3 Strengthened capacity for meteorological forecasting. • Output 4 Strengthened capacity for hydrological forecasting. • Output 5 Strengthened capacity for early warning services. • Output 6 Strengthened capacity for maintaining a sustainable institution
